items.title: Headlines for November 19, 2026 | Democracy Now!
items.excerpt: ## Trump Blasts ICC, Praises Presidents Xi and Putin at Unprecedented Trilateral Summit Nov 19, 2026 The leaders of Russia, China and the United States — Presidents Vladimir Putin, Xi Jinping and Donald Trump — have wrapped up an unprecedented trilateral summit in Shenzhen, China, with what Chinese media is calling a landmark “peace declaration.” The four-point plan calls for the three nations to reduce nuclear risks, increase oil refining, promote reforms to the United Nations and limit the jurisdiction of the International Criminal Court. This is President Trump. > President Donald Trump: “In another area of potential cooperation between us, I’ll be suggesting ways to protect our nation’s sovereignty from rogue globalist organizations such as the International Criminal Court, which has gotten out of control, which I believe we all agree has really strayed far from beyond its jurisdiction.” President Putin faces an ICC warrant seeking his arrest for war crimes committed in Ukraine, including the unlawful transfer of children from Russian-occupied areas. Neither the U.S., nor China, nor Russia is a party to the Rome Statute that established the International Criminal Court. During the summit, President Trump lavished praise on President Xi and referred to President Putin as “my friend.” That prompted Polish Prime Minister Donald Tusk to write on social media, “God, protect us from such friends.” ## Democrats Nominate Hakeem Jeffries for Speaker as Progressives Dissent on Healthcare, Gaza and ICE Nov 19, 2026 On Capitol Hill, House Democrats voted 251-11 on Wednesday to nominate New York Congressmember Hakeem Jeffries to be the next speaker of the House. Jeffries is poised to make history as the first African American to fill the role. The vote came during a closed-door caucus meeting. Afterward, seven incoming Democratic congressmembers issued a joint statement explaining their opposition to Jeffries. They wrote, “Whether on Medicare for All, stopping ICE terror, getting money out of politics, or ending the genocide in Gaza, our constituents sent us to Congress with a mandate on these issues.” ## Israeli Tanks and Bulldozers Push Past Gaza’s “Yellow Line,” Further Displacing Palestinians Nov 19, 2026 In Gaza, thousands of Palestinians have been forced to flee again after Israeli tanks and bulldozers pushed past the ceasefire’s “Yellow Line” on Wednesday and into Palestinian-held territory. Israeli troops operating east of the “Yellow Line” have gradually pushed the boundary westward and now occupy about two-thirds of Gaza’s territory, with 2 million Palestinians trapped in an increasingly narrow strip of land, most of them forced to live in tents. This is Salam Aql, a Palestinian woman who says she was displaced for the 15th time on Wednesday. ... Israeli Defense Minister Israel Katz said the military is ready to take more land and turn the newly seized areas into permanent parts of Israel’s security zones. The Palestinian Health Ministry says Israeli forces have killed over 1,600 Palestinians in Gaza since last October’s so-called ceasefire. ... ## World Court Finds Burma Committed Genocide Against Rohingya in 2017 Nov 19, 2026 Judges at the International Court of Justice have found that Burmese security forces committed genocide against Rohingya Muslims during military operations nearly a decade ago. It’s the first time the court has held a nation accountable for violating the 1948 Genocide Convention. The ruling follows the 2017 military crackdown by government forces and ethnic Rakhine mobs that killed about 10,000 people and drove more than 730,000 Rohingya into Bangladesh. ... ## Venezuela Restores Military Ties with U.S., Months After Abduction of President Maduro Nov 19, 2026 Defense Secretary Pete Hegseth made a surprise visit to Caracas on Wednesday, where he announced the U.S. and Venezuela have signed an agreement to restore military ties. Under the deal, the two countries will work together on areas such as joint training, intelligence sharing and border security. It’s Hegseth’s first visit to Venezuela since U.S. forces violently abducted former President Nicolás Maduro and his wife, National Assembly deputy Cilia Flores, back in January. The deal comes after months in which Washington has effectively controlled Venezuela’s oil sales. ... items.excerpt: Amazon's Bezos says he helped pick Pattinson as Bond Amazon founder and chairman Jeff Bezos said he was heavily involved in selecting "Batman" actor Robert Pattinson to take on the iconic film role of James Bond. Bezos spoke at Semafor's Silicon Valley & The ​World conference on Tuesday, a day after the company announced Pattinson as the next 007. ... New 'Hunger Games' prequel traces trauma behind future rebellion The new "Hunger Games" prequel explores how young Haymitch Abernathy's ordeal in ‌a deadly televised ​contest shapes him and helps sow the seeds of the rebellion against his country's oppressive rulers depicted in the later films. The films follow children, called tributes, who are forced to fight to the death in a televised spectacle staged by the rulers of the fictional nation of Panem. ... 'Choosin' Texas' singer Langley beats Taylor Swift on way to Country Music Awards sweep Ella Langley and her unstoppable hit "Choosin' Texas" dominated the Country Music Association awards on Wednesday at a ceremony that also featured Taylor Swift's first performance at the CMAs in 13 years. Swift, who began her career in country music before finding megastardom in pop, went into the show in Nashville with one ​nomination for "I Knew It, I Knew You" from the "Toy Story 5" movie soundtrack. Spain's High Court opens investigation into women's allegations against Julio Iglesias A Spanish High Court judge has opened a criminal investigation into singer Julio Iglesias after a complaint filed by two former employees alleging sexual offences, assault and degrading treatment, court records showed. The complaint was filed by rights group Women's Link Worldwide on behalf of ⁠two women who said they worked in Iglesias' Caribbean residences for 10 months in 2021, following an investigation by US broadcaster Univision and Spanish outlet elDiario.es.

items.title: Entertainment News Live Updates Today (November 19, 2026): Alia Bhatt On ‘Unequal’ Marriage With Ranbir Kapoor | Mysskin Left Keerthy Suresh Uncomfortable At Sathyavan Savithiri Press Conference | Ramayana Box Office Update - Filmibeat
items.excerpt: Actor Robert Downey Jr. revealed that he initially wondered whether there were any surprises left for him in the Avengers franchise after his character Iron Man's emotional exit in "Avengers: Endgame". Marvel Studios released a featurette featuring the Oscar winner, who discussed his decision to return to the Marvel Cinematic Universe franchise, this time playing its antagonist Victor Von Doom, also known as Doctor Doom, in the upcoming film "Avengers: Doomsday". ... ## Saif Ali Khan Receives Death Threat Bollywood actor Saif Ali Khan has reportedly received a death threat from someone claiming to be Zeeshan Akhtar, who is wanted in connection with the 2024 murder of politician Baba Siddique. The police are now trying to establish whether Akhtar was actually involved in sending the threat or if someone else used his name to target celebrities and create trouble for law enforcement agencies. This is not the first such incident reported this month. Actors Tusshar Kapoor and Ayushmann Khurrana had also received similar threats earlier. Police arrested 30-year-old Vaibhav Mishra, an IIT graduate from Bengaluru, in connection with both cases. Investigators found no links between Mishra and any criminal gang. He allegedly used artificial intelligence (AI) to send the threatening messages. ... ## Ramayana Box Office Collection Day 14 Ramayana has surpassed Aditya Dhar's Dhurandhar at the Indian box office within just two weeks of its release. According to Sacnilk, the film earned Rs. 23.20 crore net in India on Day 14, taking its total domestic net collection to Rs. 844.40 crore. Its India gross collection has now reached Rs. 1,009.05 crore. With this, Ramayana has moved ahead of Dhurandhar, which had collected Rs. 840.20 crore net in India after its release in December last year. The achievement comes just 14 days into Ramayana's theatrical run. However, the film's overseas performance appears to be slowing down. It added Rs. 8 crore gross from international markets on Day 14, taking its overseas gross collection to Rs. 510 crore. Meanwhile, its worldwide gross collection has reached Rs. 1,519.05 crore. ... Speaking to TIME magazine as part of its TIME100 Next India feature, Alia Bhatt addressed the online discussions about her marriage to Ranbir Kapoor and the claims that she is in an ‘unequal marriage’. The actress called such assumptions offensive, saying people were reducing her to someone who would silently suffer in an imaginary situation. Alia also suggested that the speculation could stem from the fact that her relationship does not follow conventional ideas of marriage. Explaining what makes her bond with Ranbir special, she said, "The bedrock of any relationship is when you feel seen without putting any effort, and feel heard without saying anything—that’s Ranbir for me, and that’s our reality."

items.title: Wake Up With BroadwayWorld November 19, 2026- IT'S A WONDERFUL LIFE: A LIVE RADIO PLAY Opens on Broadway and More
items.excerpt: The week's biggest news kicked off with a glamorous red carpet gala for IT'S A WONDERFUL LIFE: A LIVE RADIO PLAY at the Broadhurst Theatre, while Nicholas Christopher shared his journey into JUST IN TIME. Nina Ross also opened up about the personal resonance of THE UNBELIEVERS at Manhattan Theatre Club. Elsewhere, Cynthia Erivo delighted fans with a joyful dance alongside her ASL interpreter during her Lincoln Center benefit concert. Blue Man Group also made its Broadway debut with A NEW HOLIDAY SURPRISE, with highlights available in a new video, and critics have weighed in via a Review Roundup. Broadway also welcomed NOW YOU SEE ME LIVE to the Al Hirschfeld Theatre, and Hannah Cruz made her opening night debut as Audrey in LITTLE SHOP OF HORRORS at the Westside Theatre. Billy Crystal's 860 also made box office history, setting a new Imperial Theatre weekly record for a play.
